asset_heavy.reason: Operates its own candy manufacturing plants in North America with ongoing investment in advanced production equipment.

big_ticket.reason: Candy bars, pops and gum are small, frequent, low-priced purchases.

cyclical_demand.reason: Low-priced candy is bought regardless of the economy; the site says brands sell in every economic climate.

large_customers.reason: Sells candy to shoppers through stores; the retailers are mixed in size and the end buyers are households.

notes: Revenue comes mostly from sales to retailers and distributors, whose shoppers are the end consumers.

offers_products.reason: Makes and sells Tootsie Roll, Tootsie Pop, Blow Pop, DOTS, Junior Mints, Andes mints and Dubble Bubble candy.

offers_services.reason: It is a candy manufacturer, and no services appear among its offerings.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for manufactured candy, not for staff time.

recurring_revenue.reason: Retailers and vending operators reorder low-cost candy repeatedly, and consumers buy it again and again.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Consumer candy brands sold in supermarkets, drug stores and convenience stores; shoppers choose the brand.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Sells to supermarkets, warehouse clubs, dollar stores, drug stores, convenience stores and vending operators that resell the candy.
